questions.question: How does a relational database store a many-to-many relationship between two tables?
options: A list of ids inside one column of either table
A third table, the join table, holding a foreign key to each side
A copy of the second table inside the first
A single foreign key on the table that has more rows
questions.explanation: Each link between the two entities is one row in a join table that holds two foreign keys.

questions.question: Which attribute marks the inverse side of a @ManyToMany relationship?
questions.explanation: mappedBy tells Hibernate that the other class owns the join table, so this side only mirrors the link.

questions.question: A Book owns the link and has two authors. An Author named Meera is added to book1 and book2, and Arjun only to book1. After saving, how many rows does the join table book_author hold?
questions.explanation: Every link is one row: book1-Meera, book1-Arjun and book2-Meera, so the join table has 3 rows.

questions.question: A developer calls author.getBooks().add(book) on the inverse side only and saves. No row appears in the join table. Why?
options: Sets cannot be saved by Hibernate
Only changes on the owning side, the one with @JoinTable, are written to the join table
The join table is created only in production
The save method must be called twice
questions.explanation: Hibernate ignores changes made to the inverse collection, so update the owning side or use a helper that updates both.

questions.question: A many-to-many mapping uses CascadeType.ALL. Deleting one Author also deletes a Book shared with another Author. What is the fix?
options: Switch the collection to a List
Remove the cascade of remove and delete only the link
questions.explanation: Cascading remove across a many-to-many link deletes shared rows, so drop CascadeType.REMOVE and ALL.
